name: Memory Maps Anomaly
description: Reports non-ART writable, anonymous, or deleted executable mappings, smaps dirty-page code modifications, and suspicious signal handler registrations.

evidenceUnits.title: Executable mapping anomaly
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Non-ART writable, anonymous, deleted executable mappings, smaps dirty code pages, and signal handler targets
evidenceUnits.proposition: A normalized process-map entry, smaps dirty page, or signal handler target satisfies an anomaly rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/maps parsing, /proc/self/smaps dirty page audit, and sigaction query
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on maps/smaps readability and sigaction accessibility
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process map and smaps views can be filtered or rewritten
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Generic mapping anomalies have legitimate producers. Anonymous or instrumentation-owned signal handlers and writable executable mappings drive the assessment; dirty system code pages are collected as context only, because relocation and copy-on-write dirty executable pages on ordinary devices and the size thresholds are not yet calibrated against a clean baseline.
